syllabusTopics: Hydrogen: chemistry of atomic and nascent hydrogen; isotopes of hydrogen and their uses
Application of hydrogen as fuel; heavy water and its applications
Allotropes of oxygen: definition of allotropy and examples; oxygen — types of oxides (acidic, basic, neutral, amphoteric, peroxide and mixed oxides)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Carbon monoxide is chemistry's double agent. Prepared by dehydrating **formic acid with conc. H₂SO₄**, it is a colourless, odourless, water-insoluble gas with a linear triple-bonded structure and a lone pair on carbon — which makes it burn with a **blue flame** (2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂), reduce metal oxides (**Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂** in the blast furnace; I₂O₅ + 5CO → I₂ for mine-air detection), form **phosgene COCl₂**…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Carbon monoxide is a neutral oxide, a strong reducing agent, and a dangerously effective ligand for haemoglobin iron."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The garage warning sign*** — a car engine in a closed garage fills the air with CO, not CO2: incomplete combustion starves the flame of oxygen, and the victim never smells anything because CO has no odour.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Silent Killer With a Useful Streak Carbon monoxide: colourless, odourless, and — because it binds haemoglobin 200× better than O₂ — lethal at 1000 ppm. Yet the same reducing power strips oxygen from ores and feeds organic synthesis.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Preparation - Lab: **HCOOH + conc. H₂SO₄ → CO + H₂SO₄·H₂O** (dehydration of formic acid at ~140 °C); or K₂[Cu(CN)₃]... simpler: **oxalic acid + conc. H₂SO₄** gives CO + CO₂ (CO₂ absorbed in NaOH). - Incomplete combustion: 2C + O₂ (limited) → 2CO; C + CO₂ → 2CO (red-hot coke). - Industrial: water gas (C + H₂O → CO + H₂, 1000 °C) and producer gas (CO + N₂) mixtures.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Prep: HCOOH + conc H2SO4. Blue flame = CO burning. Blast furnace: Fe2O3 + 3CO. Mond: 50 C form / 230 C decompose. Phosgene COCl2 with Cl2. Hb affinity 200x. Water gas CO+H2; producer gas CO+N2.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: CO's carbon lone pair makes it a powerful ligand: the same grip that locks haemoglobin's Fe2+ shut (poisoning) also refines nickel through Ni(CO)4 and drives organometallic catalysis — one electronic feature, two opposite stories.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: CO prep: HCOOH + conc H2SO4 (140 C, dehydration); 2C + O2(limited) -> 2CO; C + CO2 -> 2CO; water gas C + H2O -> CO + H2 (1000 C); producer gas CO + N2. Properties: colourless, odourless, water-insoluble, linear bond order 3, C end negative; burns blue flame 2CO + O2 -> 2CO2.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: CO detectors are legally required in many countries because the gas gives no sensory warning at any concentration.

rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Carboxyhaemoglobin** | Hb–CO complex blocking O₂ transport | CO poisoning | | **Water gas** | CO + H₂ from steam on hot coke | fuel + synthesis gas | | **Producer gas** | CO + N₂ from air on hot coke | cheap industrial fuel | | **Phosgene** | COCl₂, carbonyl chloride | WWI gas, industrial…  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why CO is poisonous yet stable - The lone pair on carbon makes CO a strong σ-donor and π-acceptor to transition metals — haemoglobin's Fe²⁺ is simply the wrong metal to bind first. The same ligand strength that kills also drives Ni(CO)₄ refining and catalysis.…  ·  ## 5.
